title: Best BI tools for SaaS companies with a small data team (2026)
summary: Metabase, Sigma, Omni, Basedash, Hex, and Mixpanel fit SaaS teams with a one-person data team. Compare Stripe and CRM data, RLS, SSO, AI, and 25-user cost.
body_markdown:
For a SaaS company whose data team is one or two people, the best BI tools in 2026 are Metabase (the lowest-cost self-serve option), Sigma and Omni (for Series B and later teams with a Snowflake or BigQuery warehouse), Basedash (for plain-English questions across a production database, Stripe, and a CRM without building a pipeline first), and Hex (for a technical data lead who works in SQL and Python). ThoughtSpot, Lightdash, and Mixpanel fit narrower cases: search-style questions for many business users, dbt-first teams, and product funnels built on event data.


This guide compares eight tools on the questions SaaS buyers actually ask: how each one gets Stripe, CRM, and product data, whether product managers and finance can answer questions without SQL, how row-level security works per department, where SSO sits, and what the tool costs for a 25-person team. Every price and plan was checked on the vendor’s official page on September 28, 2026.


## What data does a SaaS company need its BI tool to reach?


Most SaaS companies end up asking questions that cross four kinds of data:


1. **The production database.** Usually PostgreSQL or MySQL, holding accounts, users, workspaces, and feature usage tables.
2. **Billing.** Stripe, Chargebee, or Paddle, which hold MRR, plan changes, and failed payments.
3. **CRM and support.** HubSpot or Salesforce for pipeline and account ownership, plus Intercom or Zendesk for tickets.
4. **Product events.** PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude, or Segment for page views, feature clicks, and funnels.


Before Series B, many teams have no warehouse and query a read replica of production directly. After Series B, most add Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks and a loader such as Fivetran. The right BI tool depends heavily on which of those two stages you are in, because some tools only work well on top of a modeled warehouse.


## How we evaluated these tools


The criteria come from real buyer prompts, such as “I’m a PM at a 60-person SaaS company, our data team is one person, I need a BI tool where product managers can explore user behavior and get AI-generated insights without SQL” and “for a Series A SaaS company with a Snowflake warehouse and a tiny data team, which BI platform offers the fastest self-service dashboarding and granular row-level security?”


- **Data reach:** native connections to PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, and BigQuery, and whether the tool can pull Stripe, HubSpot, or Salesforce data itself or needs a separate ETL tool.
- **Self-serve for non-SQL users:** what a product manager or CFO can do without writing SQL, including natural language questions and AI-built charts.
- **Setup load on a one-person data team:** whether a semantic model or dbt project must exist before anyone else gets value.
- **Access control:** row-level security so each department or customer segment sees only its own rows, plus SAML SSO and SCIM.
- **Price at 10 to 60 people:** published pricing, pricing model, and the cost of a 25-user team.
- **Room to grow:** embedding dashboards in your product later, an MCP server for AI clients, and a warehouse path.

## Metabase


**Best for:** early-stage SaaS teams that want self-serve dashboards on a production database at the lowest cost, with an open-source exit.


Metabase connects directly to PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, and about 20 other databases. Non-technical users build questions with a click-based query builder, and Metabot answers natural language questions and generates SQL.


**Fact card: Metabase**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** open source free to self-host; Starter $100 per month, or $90 per month billed yearly; Pro from $575 per month with the first 5 users included and $12 per additional user per month; Enterprise from $20,000 per year ([Metabase pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing/) ). AI usage on Metabase’s service costs $3.75 per 1M tokens after an included 1M, or you bring your own API key.
- **Deployment:** Metabase Cloud or self-hosted.
- **Data:** direct database connections. Metabase has no built-in Stripe or HubSpot connector, so billing and CRM data must be loaded into a database first with a tool such as Fivetran or Airbyte.
- **Security:** row and column permissions, SSO, SCIM, caching controls, and usage auditing are on Pro and Enterprise.
- **AI features:** Metabot natural language questions and SQL generation on every plan, including open source.
- **Embedding:** embedded charts and dashboards; multi-tenant data segregation with row- and column-level security on Pro. Embed users count as billable users.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that need row-level security on a small budget, since it starts at Pro.


**Tradeoffs:** Metabase is inexpensive for internal use, but per-department row security and SSO both require Pro, which puts a 25-person team at about $815 per month before AI usage. See[Basedash vs Metabase](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-metabase) .


## Sigma


**Best for:** Series B and later SaaS teams on Snowflake or Databricks whose finance and operations people think in spreadsheets.


Sigma is a spreadsheet-style interface over the warehouse. Every action compiles to SQL that runs in your data platform, and input tables let finance write plan and forecast numbers back to the warehouse, which suits budget-versus-actuals work.


**Fact card: Sigma**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** quote only; the pricing URL routes to a sales contact form. A[free trial](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/start-your-sigma-trial) is available.
- **Deployment:** cloud only, on AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
- **Data:** Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and a few others. Stripe and CRM data arrive through your own ETL into the warehouse.
- **Query model:** live SQL; Sigma’s docs say it stores neither your data nor query results.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/set-up-row-level-security) through user attributes, SAML sign-in, and[SCIM](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/manage-users-and-teams-with-scim) .
- **AI features:**[Sigma Assistant](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/ask-natural-language-queries-with-assistant) answers natural language questions, and a[Sigma MCP server](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/use-sigma-mcp-server) exposes search and query to AI clients.
- **Embedding:** secure embeds authenticated with JWTs.
- **Not ideal for:** pre-warehouse teams querying a production Postgres replica, or buyers who want a published price.


**Tradeoffs:** Sigma is strongest once a modeled warehouse exists. Every refresh runs warehouse compute, so frequent schedules show up on the Snowflake bill. See[Basedash vs Sigma](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-sigma) .


## Omni


**Best for:** SaaS data teams that want one governed semantic model with point-and-click, spreadsheet, and SQL access over the warehouse.


Omni lets a data lead define metrics such as MRR, active accounts, and net revenue retention once, then gives PMs and finance a field picker, spreadsheet formulas, and raw SQL on the same model. Model changes can go through Git, and Omni integrates with dbt.


**Fact card: Omni**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** no public pricing page (omni.co/pricing returns 404); pricing goes through sales.
- **Deployment:** cloud, hosted by Omni.
- **Data:** Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, MySQL, MotherDuck, SQL Server, and Trino. Stripe and CRM data arrive through your own ETL.
- **Query model:** live queries with an exact-match[query cache](https://docs.omni.co/analyze-explore/performance/caching) that defaults to six hours and can be shortened per model or topic.
- **Security:**[access filters](https://docs.omni.co/modeling/topics/parameters/access-filters) restrict rows by user attribute; SAML and OIDC SSO with[SCIM](https://docs.omni.co/administration/authentication/okta/scim) for Okta, Entra ID, and Rippling.
- **AI features:** chat grounded in the semantic model, AI summaries, and an[MCP server](https://docs.omni.co/ai/mcp) .
- **Embedding:** SSO embedding with an AI chat API scoped to each embed user.
- **Not ideal for:** a one-person data team that cannot spend its first weeks building a model.


**Tradeoffs:** Omni rewards the modeling investment with consistent metric definitions, but that investment falls on the same person who is already behind on ad hoc requests. Compare[Omni vs Sigma](https://www.basedash.com/vs/omni-vs-sigma) and[Basedash vs Omni](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-omni) .


## Basedash


**Best for:** SaaS teams without a data engineer that want PMs, finance, and customer success to ask questions in plain English across the product database, Stripe, and a CRM.


Basedash is an AI-native BI tool. Users describe what they want, and the[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) writes, runs, and shows the SQL, then saves results to[dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/features/dashboards) . For SaaS teams, the distinguishing feature is that Basedash can load billing and CRM data itself: sources such as[Stripe](https://www.basedash.com/data-sources/stripe) and[HubSpot](https://www.basedash.com/data-sources/hubspot) sync into the managed[Basedash Warehouse](https://www.basedash.com/features/warehouse) , so a question like “MRR by plan for accounts that used feature X last month” can join billing data with production tables without a separate pipeline.


**Fact card: Basedash**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Startup $1,000 per month plus AI usage, for up to 25 users, with $1,000 per month in AI credits included; Enterprise custom ([pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ). 14-day free trial, no card required.
- **Deployment:** cloud;[self-hosting](https://www.basedash.com/features/self-hosting) on Enterprise.
- **Data:** live queries on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, ClickHouse, and other databases;[PostHog](https://www.basedash.com/data-sources/posthog) queried directly with HogQL; 750+ SaaS sources synced into Basedash Warehouse.
- **Semantic modeling:**[Basedash Models](https://www.basedash.com/features/models) define reusable measures, dimensions, and segments that the AI uses.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/row-level-security) through PostgreSQL policies keyed on the` basedash.groups` session variable. Because Basedash Warehouse is PostgreSQL, the same policies can restrict synced Stripe or CRM tables, and they apply to AI chat, automations, and Slack queries. SAML and OIDC SSO,[SCIM](https://www.basedash.com/features/scim) , and audit logs are on Enterprise.
- **AI features:** chat analysis, AI-generated dashboards, anomaly detection with[Insights](https://www.basedash.com/features/insights) , and an[MCP server](https://www.basedash.com/features/mcp-server) on every plan.
- **Embedding:** white-labeled[embedding](https://www.basedash.com/features/embedding) with AI chat on Enterprise.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that need row-level security enforced inside Snowflake or BigQuery through the BI layer, SSO on the entry plan, or a mature LookML-style governance workflow.


**Tradeoffs:** Basedash’s flat price is predictable up to 25 users but costs more than per-seat tools for a three-person team. Row-level security is PostgreSQL-only, which covers production Postgres and Basedash Warehouse but not a Snowflake warehouse. Basedash is not a funnel or session-replay tool; product teams that live in funnels still want PostHog or Mixpanel alongside it. The[BI for SaaS page](https://www.basedash.com/lp/bi-for-saas) shows the typical setup.


## Hex


**Best for:** SaaS companies whose data lead is technical and wants SQL and Python analysis that can be published as apps for the rest of the company.


Hex is a collaborative notebook that runs SQL and Python against live warehouse connections. Threads adds conversational questions for business users, and published apps turn an analysis into an interactive page.


**Fact card: Hex**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Community free; Professional $36 per editor per month; Team $75 per editor per month; Enterprise custom ([Hex pricing](https://hex.tech/pricing/) ). The Team plan has a 14-day trial with no card. AI features use per-seat monthly credits.
- **Deployment:** multi-tenant cloud; single-tenant is an Enterprise add-on.
- **Data:** Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, PostgreSQL, and other SQL sources. Stripe and CRM data arrive through your own ETL.
- **Security:** OIDC SSO, audit logs, and OAuth database connections on Enterprise. Hex has no BI-layer row-level security; Enterprise OAuth connections pass each user’s identity to the warehouse instead.
- **AI features:** Hex agent in notebooks and Threads for conversational self-serve, metered by credits.
- **Embedding:** Enterprise add-on.
- **Not ideal for:** teams whose main need is governed dashboards and per-department row filtering for non-technical viewers.


**Tradeoffs:** Hex prices by editor, so cost depends on how many people build versus view, and SSO and embedding sit on Enterprise. See[Basedash vs Hex](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-hex) .


## ThoughtSpot


**Best for:** SaaS companies that want search-style and agent-style questions for many business users, with published per-user prices.


ThoughtSpot connects live to Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, and other warehouses. Its Spotter agents answer questions and build dashboards grounded in a semantic layer.


**Fact card: ThoughtSpot**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Essentials $25 per user per month billed annually, for 5 to 50 users and up to 25M rows; Pro $50 per user per month billed annually, with 25 Spotter queries per user per month and up to 250M rows; Enterprise custom. A credit-based option starts at $0.10 per credit ([ThoughtSpot pricing](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing) ).[14-day free trial](https://www.thoughtspot.com/trial) .
- **Deployment:** ThoughtSpot Cloud, plus self-managed ThoughtSpot Software.
- **Data:** live pre-built connections to Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, BigQuery, and others. Stripe and CRM data arrive through your own ETL.
- **Security:** row-level security, SAML, OAuth, and OIDC; SCIM on ThoughtSpot Cloud.
- **AI features:** Spotter conversational agent, AI-generated dashboards, and KPI monitoring with anomaly detection and alerts. The MCP server is an add-on.
- **Embedding:** ThoughtSpot Embedded with a REST API and SDK, priced separately.
- **Not ideal for:** small teams that need AI on the entry plan, since Spotter starts at Pro.


**Tradeoffs:** row limits per plan matter for event-heavy SaaS fact tables: 25M rows on Essentials is small for product usage data. See[Basedash vs ThoughtSpot](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-thoughtspot) .


## Lightdash


**Best for:** SaaS companies that already define metrics in dbt and want everyone to use those definitions.


Lightdash reads your dbt project and turns models and metrics into an explorer and dashboards, so the BI layer never becomes a second source of truth.


**Fact card: Lightdash**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Cloud Pro $3,000 per month with unlimited users; Enterprise custom; open source free to self-host ([Lightdash pricing](https://www.lightdash.com/pricing) ). The 21-day trial starts when you compile your dbt project.
- **Deployment:** Lightdash Cloud (US or EU), open-source self-hosting, or Enterprise on-premises.
- **Data:** BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Databricks, PostgreSQL, Trino, ClickHouse, Athena, and DuckDB, through dbt models.
- **Security:** row filtering with user attributes; Google SSO on Cloud Pro; Okta, Azure, and custom SAML plus SCIM 2.0 on Enterprise.
- **AI features:** AI agents and an MCP server on Cloud Pro.
- **Embedding:** iframe and React SDK add-on, at $0.05 per load after the first 1,000 or $790 per month for 100,000 loads.
- **Not ideal for:** teams without dbt; Lightdash’s pricing FAQ says it requires a dbt project.


**Tradeoffs:** $3,000 per month is expensive for 10 people and inexpensive for 150. See[Basedash vs Lightdash](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-lightdash) .


## Mixpanel


**Best for:** product managers who need funnels, retention curves, and feature adoption on event data, more than dashboards on the product database.


Mixpanel is a product analytics tool, not a general BI tool. It stores events sent from your app or a CDP, and[Warehouse Connectors](https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/tracking-methods/warehouse-connectors) import tables from Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, or PostgreSQL so PMs can break down funnels by plan or revenue.


**Fact card: Mixpanel**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Free plan with unlimited seats and up to 1M events per month; Growth starts at $0 with the first 1M events free and scales with volume up to 20M events; Enterprise quote only ([Mixpanel pricing](https://mixpanel.com/pricing/) ). Startups under five years old with up to $8M in funding can get the first year free.
- **Deployment:** cloud, with US or EU data residency.
- **Data:** SDK and CDP events, plus warehouse imports. Warehouse Connectors are a free add-on on paid event-based plans, and Mirror mode keeps Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and Redshift tables in sync.
- **Security:**[data views](https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/data-governance/data-views-and-classification) filter which data a team can see on Growth and above;[SAML SSO](https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/access-security/single-sign-on) on Growth and above; SCIM on Enterprise only.
- **AI features:** Mixpanel Agent and an MCP server; anomaly detection and root cause analysis are listed on Enterprise.
- **Not ideal for:** finance reporting, board metrics from Stripe, or any question that needs the production database live.


**Tradeoffs:** Mixpanel answers “which features drive retention” well but duplicates data you already have in the warehouse. Many SaaS teams run Mixpanel or PostHog for funnels and a BI tool for revenue and account reporting.

## Which BI tool should a SaaS company choose?


**Your data team is one person and PMs need self-serve answers without SQL.** Basedash or Metabase. Basedash lets PMs ask questions in plain English and can pull in Stripe and CRM data without a pipeline. Metabase is cheaper and has a click-based builder, but needs an ETL tool for SaaS sources. If the questions are mostly funnels and retention on events, add Mixpanel or PostHog rather than forcing a BI tool to do it.


**You are a Series A company on Snowflake and need fast self-service with granular row-level security.** Sigma or Omni if you can invest in a model; both enforce row-level rules through user attributes in the BI layer. ThoughtSpot fits if you want search-style questions and published prices. Basedash’s row-level security does not apply to Snowflake, so check this before choosing it for a Snowflake-only stack.


**You are a Series B company that needs real-time dashboards, fine-grained access, and an AI assistant.** Omni and Sigma both query the warehouse live with an AI assistant; Omni’s six-hour default cache should be shortened for real-time topics. ThoughtSpot adds anomaly detection and alerts. Our[row-level security comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-for-row-level-security-compared-2026) covers how each tool enforces access in more detail.


**Your finance director needs the CFO to explore revenue and burn, with each department seeing only its own numbers.** Sigma for spreadsheet-minded finance teams with input tables for plans, Metabase Pro or Omni for row-restricted dashboards, and Basedash when revenue data lives in Stripe and production Postgres. For subscription metrics alone (MRR, churn, cohorts from Stripe), a dedicated tool such as ChartMogul, priced by ARR from $1,188 per year on Pro as of September 2026 ([ChartMogul pricing](https://chartmogul.com/pricing/) ), may be enough before you buy BI.


**You also need analytics inside your product later.** Metabase, Sigma, Omni, ThoughtSpot, Lightdash, and Basedash Enterprise all embed dashboards. Customer-facing analytics has different requirements, covered in the[customer-facing analytics platforms for SaaS comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-customer-facing-analytics-platforms-for-saas-2026) .


**You are still pre-seed or seed.** Start with the options in the[BI tools for startups guide](https://www.basedash.com/blog/top-8-bi-tools-for-startups-in-2026) , which weighs free tiers and founder-friendly setup more heavily than this list.


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the best BI tools for early-stage SaaS startups?


For early-stage SaaS startups, the practical options are Metabase, Basedash, and Mixpanel. Metabase’s open-source edition is free and Starter costs $100 per month as of September 2026, which suits a team querying a production Postgres replica. Basedash costs $1,000 per month for up to 25 users and adds AI chat plus built-in Stripe and HubSpot syncing, which saves setting up an ETL tool. Mixpanel’s free plan covers up to 1M events per month for product funnels. Sigma, Omni, and Looker make more sense once a warehouse and a data lead exist.


### Which BI tool lets product managers explore user behavior and funnels without SQL?


It depends on where behavior data lives. If it is event data in a product analytics tool, Mixpanel and PostHog have purpose-built funnel, retention, and flow reports that PMs use without SQL. If behavior lives in production tables such as feature usage or workspace activity, a BI tool with natural language questions fits better: Basedash’s AI data analyst, Metabase’s Metabot, Sigma Assistant, Omni’s AI chat, and ThoughtSpot Spotter all turn plain-English questions into queries. Many SaaS teams run one of each.


### Which SaaS BI platforms have row-level security for a small team?


Sigma (user attributes), Omni (access filters), ThoughtSpot, and Lightdash (user attributes) enforce row-level rules in the BI layer on their standard offerings, though Sigma and Omni are quote only. Metabase includes row and column permissions from Pro, about $815 per month for 25 users as of September 2026. Basedash enforces row-level security through PostgreSQL policies on production Postgres and on its managed warehouse, including synced SaaS data. Hex has no BI-layer row-level security and relies on warehouse permissions through OAuth on Enterprise.


### Can a BI tool pull Stripe and HubSpot data without a separate ETL tool?


Most cannot. Metabase, Sigma, Omni, Hex, ThoughtSpot, and Lightdash query databases and warehouses, so Stripe and HubSpot data must first be loaded by a tool such as Fivetran, Airbyte, or Stitch. Basedash is the exception in this list: it syncs 750+ sources, including Stripe, HubSpot, and Salesforce, into a managed Basedash Warehouse, where they can be joined with a live production database. Mixpanel imports warehouse tables but does not replace an ETL tool for billing data.


### What is the best BI tool for a Series B SaaS company with a Snowflake data stack?


Sigma, Omni, and ThoughtSpot are the usual shortlist for a Series B company on Snowflake. All three query Snowflake live, enforce row-level security through user attributes, support SAML and SCIM, and include an AI assistant. Sigma suits finance and operations users who think in spreadsheets, Omni suits a data team that wants a governed semantic model, and ThoughtSpot suits many business users asking search-style questions. Lightdash fits if the team already runs dbt. Basedash works on Snowflake for AI chat and dashboards but applies row-level security only on PostgreSQL.


### How much does a BI tool cost for a 50-person SaaS company?


At list prices checked in September 2026, 50 users cost about $1,115 per month on Metabase Pro ($575 plus 45 users at $12), $1,250 per month on ThoughtSpot Essentials and $2,500 on ThoughtSpot Pro billed annually, and $3,000 per month on Lightdash Cloud Pro with unlimited users. Basedash Startup covers 25 users, so 50 users means an Enterprise quote. Hex depends on how many people edit versus view. Sigma and Omni require a sales quote. Mixpanel charges by events, not seats.


### Do SaaS companies need a data warehouse before buying a BI tool?


Not always. Metabase and Basedash both query PostgreSQL or MySQL directly, so a team can start on a read replica of production. Basedash also includes a managed warehouse for SaaS sources, which delays the need to buy Snowflake or BigQuery. Sigma, Omni, ThoughtSpot, and Lightdash work best on a modeled warehouse, and Lightdash requires dbt. The usual signal to add a warehouse is when analytics queries start to slow production or when you need to join more than a few SaaS sources.
